sections.label: SkillsFuture launch and SSG mission
sections.summary: SkillsFuture launched in 2014 continues an evolution, and SSG's mission is to develop an integrated training system, lifelong learning culture and employer recognition of skills.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, the launch of SkillsFuture in 2014 is a continuation of this evolution process.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: But SkillsFuture is more than just schemes and programmes to drive higher productivity and mastery, and it is certainly not just the $500 Credit; it is also about societal mindsets, and the way we value and recognise people of different talents, beyond traditional definitions of success.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: As its very name suggests, SSG's mission is to take SkillsFuture forward in the long term, by: first, developing an integrated, high-quality and responsive education and training system; second, strengthening a culture of lifelong learning and pursuit of skills mastery; and third, fostering employer recognition and ownership of skills.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We are restructuring WDA into SSG and WSG, with SSG being part of the Ministry of Education (MOE) family.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: To do so, in the immediate term, SSG will focus on five key priorities: First, we will better leverage post-secondary education institutions, in other words, autonomous universities, polytechnics and ITEs to deliver training and development for adult workers.

sections.label: SSG and PSEIs Earn-and-Learn
sections.summary: SSG will work with PSEIs to scale up the Earn-and-Learn Programme, expand workplace training and pilot cooperative education at university level.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Looking ahead, SSG will work in tandem with PSEIs to increase the scale and scope of implementation of the Earn-and-Learn Programme and facilitate more extensive workplace training and pilot the cooperative model of education at the university level.

sections.label: Progression example and accreditation harmonisation
sections.summary: A polytechnic Earn-and-Learn graduate can progress to an SIT honours degree, and SSG's fifth priority is harmonising WDA and CPE accreditation and quality assurance.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: For example, graduates from Singapore Polytechnic's Earn-and-Learn Programme leading to an Advanced Diploma in Applied Food Science will now be able to progress to SIT's Bachelor of Food Technology with Honours, with exemption from the 28-week work portion of the Integrated Work Study Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The fifth priority of SSG will be to harmonise the accreditation and quality assurance systems of WDA and the Council for Private Education (CPE) today.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: With the establishment of SSG, the regulation of the private education sector will now come under SSG.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: As a first step, SSG will cross-recognise registration and accreditation requirements for selected training providers that are currently subject to both WDA's and CPE's requirements.

sections.label: SSG annual income and expenditure estimates
sections.summary: SSG must prepare annual estimates of income and expenditure for each financial year, with separate estimates for the SDF under its charge.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: SSG will have to prepare annual estimates of income and expenditure for each financial year, with separate estimates for the SDF, which will come under the charge of SSG.

sections.label: Transfer of undertakings to SSG
sections.summary: Part Eight of the Bill transfers CPE and relevant WDA assets and liabilities to SSG, sets up a Committee for Private Education and amends related Acts.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Part Eight of the Bill concerns the transfer of undertakings from CPE and relevant parts of WDA to SSG.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Specifically, clause 66 defines and provides for the transfer of relevant assets and liabilities of CPE and relevant parts of WDA to SSG.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This includes the setting up of a Committee for Private Education under SSG to undertake its powers and functions under the Private Education Act.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: As the administration of the SDF will now come under SSG, consequential amendments are being made to the Skills Development Levy Act.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Clause 76 makes consequential amendments to the ITE Act to simplify and remove this duplication.

sections.label: SkillsFuture initiatives listed
sections.summary: The passage lists SkillsFuture Credit, Education and Career Guidance, Earn and Learn Programmes, Enhanced Internships, Individual Learning Portfolio, Study Awards, Mentoring Scheme and Sectoral Manpower Plans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Of course everybody knows the $500 SkillsFuture Credit; Education and Career Guidance (ECG) at schools; Earn and Learn Programmes (ELPs) for ITE and polytechnic students; Enhanced Internships; Individual Learning Portfolio which is coming out in 2017; Study Awards; Mentoring Scheme and Sectoral Manpower Plans.

sections.label: Bill name three areas
sections.summary: Speaker urges the Minister to consider three areas: expertise in Content, Pedagogy and Assessment, filling service gaps, and creating a 21st Century Curriculum.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: For the Bill to live up to its name, there are three areas I would urge the Minister to consider: (a) to build strong expertise in the three critical pillars of Content, Pedagogy and Assessment; (b) to become the Uber for current service gaps in some post-education spaces, for example, I will talk about a Special Education Academy in special education space; and (c) to be bold enough to Create and Chase Our Own Rainbow.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: For content, we must build a 21st Century Curriculum that provides access by individuals and businesses to new literacy subjects ‒ more than just English and Mathematics and so forth ‒ to add on, such as basic coding for some of us, or basic e-commerce for some of our businesses.

sections.label: SSG sunrise industries research
sections.summary: SSG must research, invest and build bandwidth in sunrise new industries, as e-learning and blended learning platforms are the future.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: SSG must try to research, invest and build bandwidth in "sunrise" new industries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Over the years, I have spoken at length on how e-learning platforms and blended learning platforms are the future of the day.

sections.label: MOE e-learning space
sections.summary: At the school level, MOE has promised an e-learning space.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: At the school level, MOE has promised an e-learning space.

sections.label: SSG industry assessment toolkit
sections.summary: SSG should work closely with industry to enlarge the assessment and selection toolkit, focusing more on skills and aptitude than academic results.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The SSG agency should work closely with industry to enlarge the assessment and selection toolkit so that there is more focus on skills, aptitude and not just standard academic results.

sections.label: Special needs omitted from Bill
sections.summary: The speaker is disappointed that the Bill does not mention persons with special needs or their educational needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It must include those of us who learn and contribute differently.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I am thus a little bit disappointed to see no mention of persons with special needs or their educational needs in the Bill.

sections.label: Special Education Academy model
sections.summary: The speaker advocates forming a Special Education Academy that can become the Uber or Airbnb in this learning space.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: One model that I would advocate in this regard is the formation of a Special Education Academy that can become the Uber or Airbnb in this learning space.

sections.label: Fund set aside from SDF
sections.summary: The speaker proposes setting aside a fund from the existing SDF, similar to how MediFund is set aside in the 3M healthcare system.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: To support this, I propose that a fund be set aside, very much from the existing SDF, very much like the way MediFund is set aside in the 3M system in healthcare.

sections.label: Questions on SSG and SkillsFuture
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry would require SSG to develop co-funding models, measure SkillsFuture employment outcomes, publish indicators, measure causation, and stimulate new training content.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry consider, as part of the goal-setting process for SSG, to require that the agency develop a wider variety of co-funding models whereby more extensive Government funding will be provided, perhaps on the condition of the availability of matching funding from employers, industry associations or other stakeholders to enable individuals to take up such courses that are more expensive and more extensive?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In relation to the new SSG, will the Ministry implement some process to measure the impact of SkillsFuture initiatives on the actual employment outcomes of individuals who benefit from SkillsFuture programmes?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry regularly publish such indicators for public and Parliamentary scrutiny?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: And would such measurements go beyond measuring correlation to measuring causation, that is to say, would such measurement disentangle other causative factors and focus on the impact of just the SkillsFuture programmes normalised for other causative factors?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Next, aside from assessing the quality of training in adult education, will SSG go beyond this to stimulate the development of new training and education content in Singapore and how would it do so?

sections.label: Bill takes SkillsFuture to next phase
sections.summary: It states that lifelong learning and skills mastery are promoted, and that this Bill will take SkillsFuture into its next phase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: It does so through promoting lifelong learning and skills mastery.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: This Bill will take SkillsFuture into its next phase.

sections.label: Graduates entering workforce yearly
sections.summary: Each year 40,000 to 50,000 polytechnic and university students enter the workforce, small compared to the resident workforce of over two million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Every year, 40,000 to 50,000 polytechnic and university students enter the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: But this number is small compared to the current resident workforce of more than two million people.

sections.label: Earn and Learn programme
sections.summary: The Earn and Learn programme is a key SkillsFuture initiative, a work-study programme giving fresh polytechnic and ITE graduates a career headstart.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: A key initiative under SkillsFuture is the Earn and Learn programme (ELP) which is a work-study programme to give fresh polytechnic and ITE graduates a headstart in their careers.

sections.label: Companies offering cash for courses
sections.summary: It was reported that companies offer cash or vouchers when Singaporeans sign up for courses, an indirect way of cashing out SkillsFuture Credit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: For example, it was reported that there are companies offering cash or vouchers when Singaporeans sign up for courses, an indirect way of cashing out on the SkillsFuture Credit.

sections.label: New SkillsFuture national entity
sections.summary: The passage states that a national entity will be created to give the SkillsFuture philosophy a public face and take on its name.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: This will correctly set in context what the mastering of future skills means for workers and, that is, better jobs and better lives.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It will herald the creation of an entity that will see the SkillsFuture philosophy further take shape.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is more than just bureaucratic re-shuffling because we will then have a public face to go with the name, a national entity to take on the eponym of what has already become one of the most salient aspects of Singapore life today.

sections.label: Apprenticeship training gap
sections.summary: The passage states that a large formalised apprenticeship structure was lacking and that SkillsFuture intends to plug this gap.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One of the things we did not have was a large formalised structure of apprenticeship training which would channel mid-skilled aspirants directly towards the roles in demand within specific areas, and this is one of gaps which the new SkillsFuture intends to plug.

sections.label: SkillsFuture long-term framework priority
sections.summary: The passage states SkillsFuture should prioritise a long-term overarching framework rather than short-term gains, though much focus has centred on SkillsFuture Credits.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While it may be possible for an individual to disregard relevance temporarily, for the economy as a whole, being productive without being relevant to the demands of the economy is definitely not viable.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, the SkillsFuture drive should prioritise the long-term goal of an overarching framework so as to create potential, and not be concerned only with short-term gains.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Already, an extraordinary amount of the focus of SkillsFuture has centred on the SkillsFuture Credits.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is natural, of course, and one of the stated functions of the new agency is to provide funding for the provision of adult education.

sections.label: Questions on agency priorities and performance
sections.summary: The passage asks whether productivity priorities should be qualified and how SkillsFuture and the agency's performance outcomes will be assessed.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, section 5(2)(a) of the Bill identifies Singapore workforce productivity and international competitiveness of our economy as key priorities of focus of the new agency.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Given the challenges of defining and implementing measures of productivity that are relevant and appropriate, should this not be more carefully qualified?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, given that SkillsFuture is an investment for the long term, and taking into account the multifaceted nature of the proposed agency's functions, what will be the approaches taken to assessing the performance outcomes of both the SkillsFuture movement as well as the agency?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In addition, if there are plans to implement measures of performance for SkillsFuture, will a distinction between the short-, medium- and long-term horizons be factored in?

sections.label: Productivity and future capacity shortfalls
sections.summary: The passage states that without necessary improvements, Singapore may face productivity issues and shortfalls in future productive capacity.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If we do not make the necessary 	Page: 58 improvements on this score, we may end up facing not just productivity issues, but also shortfalls in our future productive capacity.

sections.label: Malaysia computational thinking syllabuses
sections.summary: The passage states Malaysia will start incorporating computational thinking skills and computer science into school syllabuses next year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Malaysia will start incorporating computational thinking skills and computer science into their primary and secondary school syllabuses next year.

sections.label: Sharing economy opportunities for workers
sections.summary: The speaker raises that the sharing economy can bring many opportunities for mature and disabled workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I would also like to raise one particular issue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I discovered that the sharing economy can bring many opportunities for mature and disabled workers.

sections.label: Government support for mature workers
sections.summary: The Government co-pays salaries of mature and disabled workers and raised re-employment age from 65 to 67.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Our Government has done a lot in this area by co-paying the salaries of mature workers and disabled workers, and by raising the age of re-employment from 65 to 67 to encourage employers to re-employ these workers.

sections.label: Uber hearing-challenged drivers
sections.summary: Uber has some hearing-challenged drivers using technology to overcome communication barriers with passengers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Already, from what I know, Uber has some hearing-challenged drivers and they are using technology to overcome the communication barriers between them and their passengers.

sections.label: SkillsFuture training for online platforms
sections.summary: SkillsFuture could roll out training courses teaching workers to use online platforms, manage reviews and offer better services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: SkillsFuture could roll out training courses to teach them how to make use of these online platforms so that they can manage their reviews online and offer better services.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit and apprenticeship support
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether there is concerted effort for skill mastery matching economy needs and whether industry players can support apprenticeship more.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: SkillsFuture Credit given to each Singaporean is certainly a booster for individuals to come into the movement.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Having said that, is there a concerted effort to make sure that there is skill mastery that can match the current, emerging and future needs of our economy?

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In regard to the support for apprenticeship model, can the industry players play a greater role in supporting apprenticeship and on-the-job training that is applicable and transferrable within and out of the industry?

sections.label: Licensing bodies and approved courses
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether licensing bodies and industry players can play a greater role in approving courses in the Approved List of Courses.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can licensing bodies and industry players play a greater role in the approval of courses listed in the Approved List of Courses?

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, the $4 hourly allowance given to working people for attending courses may attract interest on the wrong track.

sections.label: Future skills and quality workforce
sections.summary: The passage urges awareness of future skills and jobs and says the Government is committed to developing a quality workforce for the future economy.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Let us be well-informed of what the future skills, jobs and careers are that we can look forward to and equip ourselves to be nimble and adaptable and ever ready to embrace change and brave the challenges of time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: It also shows that the Government is 100% committed to developing a quality workforce which is equipped to meet the needs and challenges of the future economy.

sections.label: Proposed SSG and courses
sections.summary: The proposed SSG is one way for the Government, and it will need to develop a wide range of courses for different interests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: On the Government's part, the proposed SSG is one good way, and it will need to develop a wide range of courses to cater to the different interests of our people.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit usage challenges
sections.summary: People know about the $500 SkillsFuture Credit but face challenges such as not knowing how to use it, lacking time or working shifts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Many people I spoke to during my worksite visits and house visits told me that they know about the $500 SkillsFuture Credit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: However, there are challenges, like not knowing how to use it, not having the time to use it or not being able to go for training courses due to work patterns like working shifts.

sections.label: Singtel and WSG collaboration
sections.summary: Singtel signed a memorandum of understanding with WSG in January this year to build a pipeline of skilled ICT and customer service professionals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: One is Singtel, which signed a memorandum of understanding with WSG in January this year, to collaborate on building a pipeline of skilled ICT and customer service professionals through programmes like Place-and-Train.

sections.label: Local graduate employment rates decline
sections.summary: MOM statistics show local university graduates' employment rate fell from 94.5% to 88.9% between 2007 and 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: MOM statistics show that between 2007 and 2015, the employment rate of local university graduates has declined, from 94.5% to 88.9%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Among these, the employment rate of graduates working full-time dropped from 89.8% to 82.4%, while the employment rate of those working part-time has risen from 4.7% to 6.6%.

sections.label: SSG and mindset change
sections.summary: Setting up the SSG, integrating basic and continuing education, and complementing society's needs are a significant mindset change for the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Although we are constantly urging SMEs to upgrade their work environment and to build up their brands, the process of transformation takes time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Thus, setting up the SSG, putting basic education and continuing education into one integrated system, and treasuring every Singaporean's social value, allowing education and training to directly complement the needs of society, are a significant mindset change for the Government.

sections.label: Manpower shortage and SSG policies
sections.summary: The speaker hopes SSG policies will look after traditional industries and SMEs, not only high value-added or emerging industries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: All of these scenarios aggravate the manpower shortage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hence, I do hope that when SSG draws up its policies, it would look after the interests of traditional industries and SMEs and not only consider the high value-added industries or emerging industries.

sections.label: MOE strategic changes and SSG
sections.summary: MOE has changed direction over the years, and with SSG it will coordinate manpower plans and lifelong learning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Looking back, MOE has undergone many strategic changes in direction, from the mode of survival in 1959, to the direction of effectiveness in 1979, on to skills in 1997, and to that of value in 2011.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Now, with the establishment of SSG, MOE will coordinate the manpower plans of all trades and industries and look after the lifelong learning journey of every individual.

sections.label: PIAAC adult skills findings
sections.summary: PIAAC found a gap between older and younger Singapore workers, with those aged 45-65 scoring below the OECD average.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Programme for the International Assessment of Adult Competencies (PIAAC), a study of adults' skills by the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD), had recently found that there is a big gap between our older and younger workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Singaporeans aged between 16 and 34 ranked second in problem-solving using digital tools, fifth in numeracy and ninth in literacy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Those aged 45-65 scored lower than the OECD average.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: They ranked 31st in literacy and numeracy skills and 18th for problem-solving.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The survey also found that about 12% of Singapore adults had no prior experience with computers, compared to the OECD average of 10%.

sections.label: Changing job market and workforce
sections.summary: The job market is changing fast, so the workforce must develop skills for the future and plan for manpower needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The job market is changing in ways and at a speed not seen in the past.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is of utmost importance to ensure that the Singapore workforce continue to develop "skills for the future" and be well-prepared to predict and plan for medium- to long-term manpower needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Today's workforce is also different, as young people spend the earlier part of their career on a journey of self-discovery.

sections.label: Private institutions and course quality
sections.summary: Private institutions may take in more students at the expense of course quality, and the speaker asks about checks on inflated fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Private institutions can quickly take advantage of the influx of Government funding for their courses, taking in more students at the expense of the quality of their courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will there also be checks in place to ensure that course providers do not inflate their course fees?

sections.label: Measuring student satisfaction
sections.summary: The speaker asks if a mechanism will measure students' satisfaction with courses and course providers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In light of clause 5(1)(i), to improve the quality of courses, can the Minister clarify if a mechanism will be put in place to measure the students' levels of satisfaction for the course and course provider?

sections.label: SSG functions and powers
sections.summary: SSG's functions and powers complement WSG's, focusing on skills acquisition, lifelong learning, training provider accreditation and private education regulation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The functions and powers of SSG complement that of WSG, where SSG will focus on the facilitation of skills acquisition and lifelong learning, as well as the accreditation and assurance of training providers, and the regulation of the private education sector.

sections.label: Including established PEIs in SkillsFuture
sections.summary: The Ministry is urged to include well-established PEIs with accredited programmes and high graduate employment rates in SkillsFuture initiatives and training.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In clause 5(1)(d), I urge the Ministry to consider including, as part of SkillsFuture initiatives and training, PEIs that are more well-established and have proven track records of accredited programmes and qualifications, as well as high employment success rates of their graduates.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: There are programmes and certification courses in these PEIs which are attractive to skills upgraders and which add diversity to the post-secondary and tertiary education landscape.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It is important to ensure the quality of programmes and include only PEIs that are well-accredited and have high employment or career progression rates for their graduates.

sections.label: Appointing SSG members
sections.summary: The Ministry is urged to appoint SSG members with a good mix of academic qualifications, industry experience including private sector, and overseas work experience.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For clauses 9 and 10, I urge the Ministry to appoint members of SSG who are of a good mix.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: They should not just be academically qualified, but also have substantial industry experience, including that from the private sector, and of having worked overseas.

sections.label: Real wage growth 2011 to 2015
sections.summary: Real wage in Singapore grew 1.1% per year from 2011 to 2015, which many people may not be aware of.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Many people may not be aware that the real wage in Singapore has grown 1.1% per year from 2011 to 2015.

sections.label: Real productivity growth 2011 to 2015
sections.summary: Real productivity growth was only 0.4% per year in the same period from 2011 to 2015.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: At the same time, we must not forget that real productivity growth was at only 0.4% per year in the same period.

sections.label: SkillsFuture credits for professional qualifications
sections.summary: Residents say available courses are not what they want, and SkillsFuture credits cannot be used for certain professional qualifications like Certified Internal Auditor and Certified Information System Auditor.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And the courses that are available are not those that they want.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So, according to my residents, SkillsFuture credits cannot be used for certain professional qualifications like Certified Internal Auditor and Certified Information 	Page: 69 System Auditor.

sections.label: SkillsFuture credits used
sections.summary: About 18,000 people used their credits in the programme's first three months.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: About 18,000 used their credits in the first three months of the programme.

sections.label: SkillsFuture covers traditional jobs
sections.summary: SkillsFuture is for traditional skills and industries as well as new industries, not only future skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I want to start with Mr Melvin Yong's comment about the worker who saw the video and said, "My job is not in there", and also Mr Thomas Chua's point that there are still many traditional jobs, 	Page: 70 "还有很多传统的工作".

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, SkillsFuture is not about, as what the Chinese translation sometimes says, "未来技能", that is, literally, "skills for the future".

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: SkillsFuture is for both traditional skills, traditional industries, as well as for new industries that are going to come up.

sections.label: SkillsFuture applies to everybody
sections.summary: SkillsFuture is applicable to everybody, whether in traditional sectors or new sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: SkillsFuture is applicable to everybody, whether in traditional sectors or in new sectors.

sections.label: MOE industry needs measures
sections.summary: MOE pays attention to industry needs and introduced compulsory internships in ITE and polytechnics and ELP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: MOE (Higher Education) pays a lot of attention on industry needs, and we know that we must do this better over time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We have introduced (a) compulsory internships in ITE and polytechnics, even overseas internships; and (b) ELP.

sections.label: Expanding ELP to adults
sections.summary: CSIP is chaired by Tharman Shanmugaratnam, and a suggestion to expand ELP to adult workers will be looked into.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And of course, at the apex, we have the CSIP, where industry leaders are also represented, which is chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Tharman Shanmugaratnam.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: There is a suggestion from Mr Desmond Choo that we have an ELP scheme now, but it is catered mostly to the young and not to adult workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I think it is a very valid suggestion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: This is definitely an area that we want to look into – how we expand ELP, not just for the young, fresh graduates from ITE or the polytechnics, but also for adult workers who have worked for a few years and want to do an ELP to upgrade themselves with higher qualifications.

sections.label: Cooperative programmes pilot projects
sections.summary: More cooperative programmes are being rolled out, with first pilot projects expected next year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, we try to achieve this as we roll out more cooperative programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We expect the first few pilot projects to be rolled out next year.

sections.label: Union network guiding workers
sections.summary: Unions and their resources could help guide workers on training, development and using their $500 SkillsFuture Credit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: If we can get the whole union network and all their resources to help reach out and guide workers on how to go about their training and development, how to make use of their SkillsFuture Credit of $500, I think that is powerful.

sections.label: National Silver Academy for seniors
sections.summary: A National Silver Academy offers over 500 courses and 10,000 learning places for Singaporeans aged 50 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We will try to do more for seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We have set up a National Silver Academy where there are more than 500 courses and 10,000 learning places in there − in IT, finance, arts, design − and catered to Singaporeans aged 50 and above.

sections.label: SG Enable and SEN support
sections.summary: SG Enable courses are in the SkillsFuture Credit directory, and every Government-funded university, polytechnic and ITE has a Special Education Needs support office.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: SG Enable courses have been included into the SkillsFuture Credit course directory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, for persons with disabilities, they can use their $500 for those courses and if there are more suggestions, we will include them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Third, we have opened a Special Education Needs support office in every Government-funded university, polytechnic and ITE.

sections.label: Other training providers' courses
sections.summary: Other training providers deliver courses listed in the SkillsFuture Credit course directory, which now has over 15,000 courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The last layer of partners includes other training providers that deliver courses that are listed in the SkillsFuture Credit course directory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: There are over 15,000 of these courses now.

sections.label: WDA Individual Learning Portfolio portal
sections.summary: WDA is developing an Individual Learning Portfolio (ILP) portal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: WDA is developing an Individual Learning Portfolio (ILP) portal.

sections.label: Portal ready next year
sections.summary: It may be ready sometime next year, giving an additional mechanism to curate the course directory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Hopefully, it will be ready sometime next year and then we will have an additional mechanism to curate the course directory.

sections.label: Training versus industry need
sections.summary: The passage asks whether training people for degrees fuels their desire for degrees or addresses industry need, noting work with the top six biggest PEIs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: If you train people, you educate them to have a degree, are you just fuelling their desire for a degree, or are you trying to answer and address an industry need?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We have done some work on this with the top six biggest PEIs.

sections.label: Training and wage outcomes study
sections.summary: A 2012 study found econometrically that more training led to better wage outcomes and full qualifications led to even better outcomes, though causality cannot be claimed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But even if there is correlation, we cannot claim causality; it is hard to claim causality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: They established, econometrically, that more training did lead to better wage outcomes and that obtaining full qualifications resulted in even better wage outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: This was a one-time fairly big study done in 2012.

sections.label: Sector KPIs for competitiveness
sections.summary: Each sector develops its own KPIs to measure its competitiveness and productivity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Each sector develops their own KPIs to measure their competitiveness as well as their productivity.

sections.label: SkillsFuture as societal evolution
sections.summary: SkillsFuture is described as not just an evolution in education and training but also an evolution in society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: SkillsFuture is, therefore, not just an evolution in education and training, but also an evolution in society.

sections.label: Training for prisoners
sections.summary: The passage asks whether SSG will work with the Ministry of Home Affairs to push training to prisoners serving sentences, noting e-learning opportunities for vulnerable groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: My question is: will SSG give some thought to working with the Ministry of Home Affairs to see how we can push out training to prisoners actually serving their sentence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: In other countries, you hear stories of people earning their degree when they are in prison.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I think we already have a good working relationship and this is certainly something that we will continue to work on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: With Internet, with e-learning, actually the opportunity for everyone to learn, wherever you are, including from prison, becomes more available, with all these technologies that we can leverage on to reach out to many more vulnerable groups, including prisoners who are still serving their sentence.      .
